note_on_method: Two kinds of claim appear below and they are kept apart deliberately. Claims about the world - how many courts a park has, whether it is lit, when it opens - come from the City of San Antonio and are cited. Claims about our own coverage are facts about this dataset rather than about Bexar County, and are worded so a reader cannot mistake one for the other. San Antonio is the only city of Bexar County on this page.

slots.coverage: One city in Bexar County is published here: San Antonio, with eight venues and forty-three courts verified against the City of San Antonio's own pages. It is the first city in Bexar County on this site and the second in Texas, after Austin. Bexar County also has its own parks, and a ring of incorporated suburbs - Alamo Heights, Leon Valley, Converse, Schertz and others - and not one of those has been read against a named source, so none appears anywhere on this site and this page does not characterise them. What it reports is eight City parks whose count sentences, addresses, hours and, at two of them, lighting the City publishes and we have read. Two venues inside San Antonio itself are absent and named rather than dropped. Piazza Italia Park has "one outdoor pickleball court" and an address, "500 Columbus", that neither the US Census address file nor OpenStreetMap can find. Hamilton Community Center, at 10700 Nacogdoches Rd., has facility hours and a Saturday pickleball window and no court count anywhere. Each is one fact short of publishing, and neither fact is about the courts being real. The City's directory also says "11 Result(s) Found" and serves ten, so there may be a further listed venue that has not been read; it is not guessed at.
slots.distribution: What is verified in this county is concentrated in one city and, within it, in one park. Fairchild Park's eighteen lighted outdoor courts are eighteen of the county's forty-three - the second-largest single-venue count on this site after Mesa's Tennis & Pickleball Center, and the largest anywhere here where the operator states every court is both lit and outdoor. Monterrey holds eight and Tejeda six; the other five parks hold eleven between them, and three of those five have two courts or fewer. Geographically the eight sit on every side of San Antonio the City names - Fairchild and Pittman-Sullivan on the east, Garza and Monterrey on the west, Normoyle, Palm Heights and Tejeda on the south and south-west, Oak Haven on the north - but the courts do not: twenty-four of the forty-three are at two parks, Fairchild on the east side and Tejeda on the south. The useful split is the one the City writes into its sentences. Thirty-five courts are stated outdoor, two are stated indoor at Palm Heights, and six at Tejeda are stated lit but neither indoor nor outdoor. Twenty-four courts across two venues are lit; the other six venues carry no lighting answer under the directory's caveat that "Some courts are not lighted." Every park runs 5 a.m. to 11 p.m. daily, first come, first served. No price is stated anywhere, so no court in Bexar County is published as free, and no surface is stated for any of them.
slots.gaps: The honest position is that this is a San Antonio page wearing the heading of a county, and a San Antonio page that covers one operator. Bexar County's own parks have not been read. Alamo Heights, Leon Valley, Converse and Schertz have not been read. Nothing outside a municipal parks department appears here at all - no club, no school, no commercial venue - and that is a fact about who publishes a checkable page, not about where the game is played. The threshold has not moved: three venues with a named source and a date. Within San Antonio the gaps are of a specific kind. The City states no price at any park; "first come, first served" is how you get a court, not what it costs, and these pages do not turn a silence into "free". It states no surface. It states lighting for pickleball at two parks and warns that "Some courts are not lighted", which leaves six venues and nineteen courts with no lighting answer, seventeen of them outdoors, until the City says otherwise. And it states "outdoor" or "indoor" at seven parks and not at Tejeda, whose six courts are the only ones in the county with no breakdown. There is also a gap in the record itself. The City's site answered a plain request with 200 and, twenty minutes later, 403, so its pages are fetched with a browser header set; a 403 is a fact about one day, and every quoted sentence is re-asserted on every build. Hamilton Community Center's own page was one of those refusals, which is why its line on the directory is all this site knows of it.

faqs.q: How many pickleball courts are there in Bexar County?
faqs.a: We do not know, and no honest page can tell you. What we have checked is 43 courts across eight venues, all City of San Antonio parks, each with a source and a date you can see. The City itself lists two more pickleball sites we cannot publish, and nothing outside the City has been read.

faqs.q: Why is only San Antonio listed?
faqs.a: Because it is the only operator in the county whose courts we have confirmed against a named source. A city appears here once three or more of its venues carry a source_url and a date_checked. Bexar County's own parks and the suburbs - Alamo Heights, Leon Valley, Converse, Schertz - have not been read, so this page says nothing about them.

A count sentence on each park's own page that carries the words that matter - "There are 18 lighted, outdoor pickleball courts." - plus a directory that gives every park an address, park hours of 5 a.m. to 11 p.m., and the first-come, first-served rule. San Antonio is one of the few operators here that writes "outdoor" or "indoor" into the count itself.

faqs.q: Are the courts on this page free?
faqs.a: Not stated, at any of the eight. The City says its courts are first come, first served, which is a play format rather than a price, and no page states a charge or the absence of one. This site records a fee only when an operator publishes it, so nothing in Bexar County is published as free.

Fairchild Park, with 18 lit outdoor courts, and Tejeda Park, with 6 lit courts - both because "lighted" is in the City's own count sentence. The other six venues carry no pickleball lighting answer, and the City's directory warns that "Some courts are not lighted", so they are recorded as unknown.

We do not know. The City's pickleball directory says "11 Result(s) Found" and lists ten - nine parks and Hamilton Community Center - and its second page returns the same ten. That line is asserted on every build so a change is noticed, and the eleventh venue is not guessed at.

faqs.q: How often is this checked again?
faqs.a: These pages were read on 7 September 2026, and every one of them is snapshotted into the repository that builds this site and re-asserted on every build. If the City changes a count, adds "outdoor" to Tejeda's sentence, or publishes a court count for Hamilton, the build fails and someone reads the page again.

sources.publisher: City of San Antonio Parks & Recreation
sources.evidence: The City's pickleball directory page. Intro: "There are several indoor and outdoor pickleball courts at our parks across the city. These are available on a first-come, first-served basis. Some courts are not lighted." Then "Courts at Hamilton Community Center are available Saturday, 10 a.m. - 2 p.m." and "All other courts are available during park hours." and "Want to learn how to play? Take a Pickleball 101 class through the Fitness in the Park program, equipment provided." Under "Directory" it says "11 Result(s) Found" and lists ten entries, each park with its address and "Park Hours: Sunday - Saturday: 5 a.m. - 11 p.m."; Normoyle Park additionally "Pool Hours: Saturday & Sunday: 1 - 8 p.m."; Hamilton Community Center at "10700 Nacogdoches Rd., San Antonio, TX 78217" with "Facility Hours: Monday - Thursday: 10 a.m. - 8 p.m. Friday: 2 - 6 p.m. Saturday: 10 a.m. - 4 p.m." and no count; Piazza Italia Park at "500 Columbus, San Antonio, TX 78207". "Page 1 of 2", and page two returns the same ten. Snapshot: data/sources/san-antonio/pickleball.html
sources.not_stated: Any court count, any price, any surface, which courts are the unlit ones, and the eleventh result.

sources.evidence: Tejeda Park's page. Park History: "The 8.7570 acres of property for this park were purchased in 1977. The park was originally called Division Park for the street on which it is located, but was renamed for Congressman Frank Tejeda by ordinance of City Council passed on Sept. 12, 1996." Tejeda "was a U.S. Marine and Vietnam veteran who earned the Bronze Star for valor and the Purple Heart", "earned a masters from Harvard University and his law degree from Yale", served in the Texas House from 1977, the Texas Senate from 1987, and the U.S. House for District 28 from 1993; "He died of brain cancer on Jan. 30, 1997". Featured Amenities: "Pickleball Courts: There are 6 lighted, pickleball courts." "Tennis Courts: The tennis courts are lighted." Softball Field for rental. Amenity list includes Bleachers, Dugouts, Handicapped Parking Spaces, Regular Parking Spaces, Restrooms, Tennis Court. Address "541 Division Ave. San Antonio, TX 78214". Hours "Sunday - Saturday: 5 a.m. - 11 p.m." Snapshot: data/sources/san-antonio/tejeda-park.html
